Short-Term Memory

Ever walked into another room to get something, only to arrive and completely forget why you went there? You look around, but your mind’s gone blank. Don’t panic—it’s not a sign of memory loss. It’s just your brain doing its thing.

Why does it happen?
Your brain treats moving from one room to another like a scene change, clearing some of its temporary “drafts.” On the way, your attention may wander to random thoughts—and suddenly you’re solving the fate of humanity instead of remembering to grab your charger. Your brain also saves energy by letting small, short-lived details go.

What can you do?
Before you leave, say out loud: “I’m going to get my phone.” That helps your brain lock in the task. You can even make it a little ritual and narrate your journey like a sat-nav: “Route set. Destination: fridge.” Fewer chances of freezing in the doorway like a character in a video game.
